summary.en: Colombia is grappling with a deadly earthquake that has left more than 224 people dead while Colombian mercenaries are being targeted in Ukraine, where a Russian strike hit a major deployment hub. The UN has urged De la Espriella to uphold the peace agreement, and a U.S. indictment has revived former FARC leader Timochenko’s name in a Venezuelan case, showing the conflict’s cross‑border dimension. These developments add external shock and legal pressure to the internal violence that still produced 225 battle‑related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Colombia sliter med et dødelig jordskjelv som har tatt livet av mer enn 224 personer, mens colombianske leiesoldater blir mål i Ukraina, der et russisk angrep traff et stort utplasseringsknutepunkt. FN har oppfordret De la Espriella til å overholde fredsavtalen, og en amerikansk tiltale har gjenopplivet navnet til tidligere FARC‑leder Timochenko i en venezuelansk sak, noe som viser konfliktens grenseoverskridende dimensjon. Disse utviklingene tilfører ekstern sjokk og juridisk press til den interne volden som fortsatt har forårsaket 225 kamprelaterte dødsfall i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Colombian conflict
background.extract: The Colombian conflict began on May 27, 1964, and is a low-intensity asymmetric war between the government of Colombia, paramilitary groups, crime syndicates, and far-left guerrilla groups engaged in armed factional hostilities to increase their influence in Colombian territory. Some of the most important international contributors to the Colombian conflict include multinational corporations, the United States, Cuba, and the drug trafficking industry.
